correctness.rationale: Conditional on its uniform arrival time x, a tagged long edge pivots precisely if its b-1 companions have arrived and all m short paths remain incomplete. Integrating and aggregating gives the beta integral and product. For the normalized Banzhaf calculation the analogous independent-coalition factors give the short-to-long per-edge ratio (2^b-1)/(2^a-1); summing over ma short edges and b long edges gives the displayed share. The Shapley integrands differ by the strictly positive x^(a-1)(1-x^a)^(m-1)(1-x^(b-a)). With A=b/a and T=a(2^b-1)/(b(2^a-1)), the adjacent difference in (2^n-1)/n^2 has strictly positive numerator for n>=2, so T>A and R_1>1. The sign of R_(m+1)/R_m-1 is the opposite of A-T+(A-1)mT, strictly increasing in m, hence any plateau is at the peak above one. The gamma ratio yields R_m of order m^(1-A), which tends to zero; the boundary has at most one tie. Seven is minimal within the stated family after adding a short path since m>=2 and 2a+b>=7, not a claim about all simple graphs. New exact permutation and coalition enumeration verified both minimal-witness fractions and the 1/6 tie. The frozen certificate reports finite checks only; its 17040 pivotal count is the nominal total of edge/other-edge subsets, while the code skips states already winning, not 17040 separate swing evaluations. This accounting detail does not affect its fractions or the theorem.
